source: Real headless conversions via scripts/cli-convert.mjs -w pyrite on 2026-08-22. Document: IM MCQ Exams 2024-193.pdf, 12 pages, CamScanner scan of a Cairo University internal medicine paper. Two sections that each restart numbering at 1, and a photographed handwritten answer key bound in as page 12.
shape: sectioned; restarting labels; bound-in answer key; scanned; no figures
gold_comparison: Not run on this document. The 0.1.0 row below is the same workflow before this change, not a Gold baseline.

runs.notes: 20 questions lost in local assembly, not extraction: every one of the 45 was present in the raw window responses. Section B's labels 1-20 collided with Section A's under a document-wide label key and the loser was discarded unflagged. Two complete questions were corrupted into 8-option hybrids by a continuation attaching to the wrong stem. The 4 answers came from the key page leaking into the last window as a look-ahead.
Same six requests. All 45 answers read off the bound-in key page by the extraction request that already covered it.

gate.ambiguous_rows_flagged: pass on this document (nothing left ambiguous)

caveats: One document, two runs of the new code and one of the old. This is a data point, not a benchmark sweep.

An intermediate run of 0.2.0 exposed model variance the first run hid: printed labels came back as '15)' in some windows and '15' in others. Normalizing them is part of 0.2.0; the shape of that variance is why a single run cannot prove a merge fix.
The separate answer-key PDF path is now section-scoped but still has no end-to-end verification on a real key document.
No figure-heavy case exercised; Pyrite does not detect figures by design.
